label: Ground temperature at 1 m, mid-century
description: GIPL 2.0 mean annual ground temperature at 1 m, where ESA shows permafrost
details: 2040–2069 · 5-model average · RCP 4.5 · outside the ESA permafrost zone counts as Low
method: Mean annual ground temperature at 1 m depth from GIPL 2.0 (SNAP, 1 km EPSG:3338), 5-model average, RCP 4.5, averaged over climate years 2040–2069. The GIPL files are labelled 20 years late (file year = climate year + 20). Only cells where ESA CCI Permafrost v5 shows permafrost in 2023 (permafrost fraction above 0) get a value; everywhere else there is no permafrost to thaw and the class is always Low. Inside that zone, cells with stuck GIPL values, and a 2 km border around them, are removed (no value).
pros: Simple to explain: how warm the ground at 1 m will be
GIPL's 0 °C line at 1 m matches field sites well (best split −0.2 °C, CUSP)
cons: Single cells are uncertain by up to about 2 °C, and by mid-century half of all cells sit within 0.5 °C of a class edge (zero curtain): unstable classes
Level only: says nothing about how fast things change
Stuck GIPL cells have no value (14 % of the Interior)
sources: ESA CCI Permafrost v5 PFR 2023 (features_1km.nc pfr_2023)
author: Joshdpaul
